review_notes: Scope decision: the principal question is whether balance-sheet and cash-flow discretionary-accrual measures lead to different earnings-management inferences when the partition coincides with a non-articulation event. The paper describes this as its most significant finding, and Table 3 Panel B directly tests it. Retained six annual specifications: two primary accrual measures crossed with three partition indicators. Excluded Table 3 Panel A bias calculations, Table 2 accrual-measurement-error characterization, and later Tables 4–6 and portfolio applications.

Each Table 3 Panel B specification is estimated separately by year from 1988 through 1997. The All Years row summarizes ten annual estimates; it is not a pooled regression. The 14,558 firm-years is the overall sample, not any single annual regression N.

Retained six year-by-industry modified-Jones construction fits because their estimated coefficients generate the NDACC components of the retained DACC outcomes. The fits use firm-years without the specified non-articulation event and apply the parameters to ΔRev−ΔAR and PPE. Footnote 12 distinguishes balance-sheet and cash-flow sources of ΔAR.

Applied Section II event definitions to the generic Table 3 PART notes: Compustat annual footnote code #1 for M&A; Compustat #66 discontinued operations greater than $10,000; and Compustat #150 foreign-currency gain/loss greater than $10,000. The body’s more specific item-code and threshold rules refine the table definitions rather than conflict with them.

The Table 3 equations and Equation (1) are supported by coordinator-verified transcriptions appended to the assigned reading. Equations (10a/b) and (11a/b) are readable in the supplied page text with damaged Greek labels only; no worker-created transcription was added to the reading.

Table 3 Panel A is used only for the reported standard deviations of retained PART indicators. Its bias estimates and correlations are outside the selected baseline results.
